references.text: Joshua also gathers here the elders of Israel, the heads, judges, and officers, as a parallel to the assembly in chapter 24.
Shechem was an important place where Abraham first received the promise of the land, and where Joshua now gathers the people to renew the covenant.
Jacob came to Shechem and built an altar there, which makes the place significant for Israel's covenant history.
Jacob gathered his family in Shechem to remove foreign gods, a thematic parallel to Joshua's call to choose whom they will serve.
Moses gave command concerning blessing and cursing at Shechem, which Joshua now completes through the renewal of the covenant.
Moses instructed about a covenant ceremony in the Shechem area, which Joshua now carries out.
Moses gathered the elders of the people at Sinai for the conclusion of the covenant, corresponding to Joshua's gathering of the leaders in Shechem.
Stephen refers to Shechem in his speech about Israel's history and connects the place with the graves of the patriarchs.
